what_happened: An operator rebuilt Athena from the work branch by hand before landing job 20261025-001232-vesh. The job added a new [history] cutover_job field to athena.toml. The installed build did not know that field and refused the config as having an unknown field. The job could not be landed with `athena land` until the operator rebuilt the binary.
cause: The landing path parses athena.toml with the installed binary's schema, which is the build before the job. A job that changes the schema and the config together can never be read by its own lander. Nothing detects this case ahead of landing, and there is no sanctioned bootstrap path such as landing with the work-branch build. The existing config-ahead-of-schema class covers admission refusal. This is the landing-time version. The stale-binary and self-landing-bootstrap classes cover related but different symptoms. The rebuild left no record and no check that the operator built the right commit.
prevention: Add a sanctioned bootstrap path to landing. When a job's diff changes the config schema or the config fields, `athena land` should detect that the installed build cannot parse the post-change athena.toml. It should then either build and run the land from the verified work-branch commit, or refuse with a clear message that names the command to run. It should record the rebuild as a logged step. Landing should also parse the post-change config with the job's own build before it attempts the merge. Config readers should ignore unknown fields in landing-only paths, or the config version should be checked explicitly.
proposed_request: Make `athena land` work for a job that changes the athena.toml schema together with its config. Before merging, land should check whether the installed build can parse athena.toml as it will be after the job. If it cannot, land should build Athena from the verified work-branch commit in a temporary location, confirm that the commit matches the verified head, and run the landing with that build. It should write the normal records and add a record saying a bootstrap build was used. If it cannot build, it should refuse with a message saying exactly what to run. Acceptance: (1) a test lands a job that adds a new [history] field unknown to the installed build, and the landing succeeds with records written; (2) a test shows that a mismatched work-branch commit is refused; (3) a landing that needs no schema change behaves as before; (4) the bootstrap record is visible in `athena` status output. Link this to open request 20261016-223813-tcn9 and do not duplicate its admission-time change.
